purpose: Test whether the nested bare-bed counterfactual subset is geographically plausible before field deployment, using 2024 SWFWMD seagrass polygons and already-open recent sampling-state data only.

source.seagrass_dataset: FWC/FWRI Seagrass Florida current statewide compilation
source.tampa_provenance: FWC metadata states that the current southwest-Florida component incorporates SWFWMD Seagrass in 2024; the statewide compilation retains the most recent mapped source where datasets overlap.
source.node_registry: Pinned TBISMP Event/Occurrence snapshot, latest eligible 2023-2025 state
source_delivery_history: Direct SWFWMD MapServer metadata was accessible but its query endpoint returned non-JSON/empty responses in GitHub Actions on two frozen-rule attempts.
The physical GIS source was therefore switched before obtaining any spatial-feasibility result; no distance/sample threshold was changed.

frozen_rules.edge_definition: distance from fixed node to boundary of the union of mapped 2024 seagrass polygons
frozen_rules.outside_polygon_rule: A historically/recently vegetated transect outside the 2024 mapped union is flagged as a map-state mismatch, not automatically treated as a valid bare control.

pass_rule: At least 12 recent vegetated nodes have a mapped meadow edge within 100 m, with at least 3 such nodes in each core bay. The 18-node target is planning, not a pass requirement.
claim_boundary: This is field-feasibility only; it is not an ecological mechanism test.
A mapped edge within 100 m does not prove a depth-matched bare control exists.
The 0.25-acre mapping unit can miss small unvegetated gaps inside patchy beds, so failure is conservative and requires field/imagery reconnaissance rather than threshold relaxation.
Do not use future Thalassia response to choose bare controls.
The FWC statewide compilation is used for spatial feasibility, not for Tampa seagrass time-series inference.
